parts.note: reads as the arrangement of springs in a bed or mattress, but means a taut sprung canvas sheet that gymnasts bounce on

explanation.surface: A question about how the springs are arranged inside a mattress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the coiled metal in a bed; here the whole thing is a springy mat you bounce on, laid out like a bed in a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The apparatus is a sprung canvas sheet in a frame, used for bouncing, a bed-like layout built for springing.

definitions.meaning: strips of fabric used to tie things up

explanation.surface: Records of the ties a man wears.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic recordings and binding strips are both narrow bands of material.

definitions.meaning: in solo whist, a bid to make nine tricks
read as a dance involving a cake, a bun dance

explanation.surface: Someone sings a solo for an easy dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Solo whist is a card game whose bids include this one; the second reading splits the word as A BUN DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid of nine tricks in solo whist bears this name, and split up it describes a dance with a bun.

clue.text: Like one of Old Possum's Cats, No. 53 thinks he's funny

parts.words: Like one of Old Possum's Cats
parts.note: T. S. Eliot's book is Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats
the 53rd card in a pack, after the 52 ordinary ones, is the wild card with a jester on it

explanation.surface: Cat number 53 in Eliot's book believes itself amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: A full pack has 52 cards plus the extra wild card, number 53.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster who plays tricks on people is someone who believes himself amusing.

clue.text: Lincoln in German song of a sluggard

indicators.note: in puts the president's name inside the German word for a song

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song
Abe is Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: Lincoln appears in a German song about a lazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays in bed late is a lazy person, a sluggard.

clue.text: Ten rats might well have spoilt these in Hamelin

definitions.text: Ten rats might well have spoilt these in Hamelin

indicators.note: spoilt tells us the letters of the two words are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: Hamelin's rats ruined the townsfolk's chats.
explanation.walkthrough: In Browning's Pied Piper the rats were 'spoiling the women's chats'; 'spoilt' rearranges TEN RATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chats and gossip are what Browning's Hamelin rats spoilt.

parts.note: wan means pale and sickly-looking
D is the old abbreviation for a penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A description of a rod of pale copper metal.
explanation.walkthrough: In pre-decimal British money d stood for a penny, the copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's or conductor's slender stick is a rod.

parts.note: looks like a district of the city of Rochester, but means the French girl in Mr Rochester's care in Jane Eyre

explanation.surface: An electoral district of Rochester.
explanation.walkthrough: Rochester is the master of Thornfield in Jane Eyre; Jane is hired to teach his young ward.
explanation.definitionFit: In Charlotte Brontë's novel the little French girl Jane tutors is Mr Rochester's ward.

definitions.meaning: read as ..., with sol the Latin for sun

explanation.surface: Feeling miserable from lack of sunlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched and forsaken means forlorn; split up the word suggests the sun has been taken away.

parts.note: reads as selecting a key from a ring of them, but means the very best of a group

explanation.surface: A selection made from a ring of keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a door key chosen from a bunch; read as 'key' meaning prime, it is the best choice.
explanation.definitionFit: The finest of a group is the selection anyone would make first.

clue.text: Best time for feathering one's nest?

definitions.text: Best time for feathering one's nest?

parts.note: a plum is the best of something, as in a plum job
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: When is the ideal moment for making oneself rich?
explanation.walkthrough: To feather one's nest is to grow rich, but read literally a bird's nest is lined with feathers, and the whole clue points to a bird's coat of feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's covering of feathers is its feathering, the stuff a nest is lined with.

clue.text: Muscle in here a jiffy with some final words

parts.note: in a trice means in a jiffy, an instant
PS, postscript, is the words added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Flexing an arm muscle in no time, plus a few closing remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in here' just leads into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the large three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm.

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a table is a list of figures or names

explanation.surface: A team sheet pinned up in the dining-room.
explanation.definitionFit: A serving table set against the wall is a piece of furniture found in a dining-room.

clue.text: Sound of a bell Miss Trent heard

indicators.note: heard means the name is taken as spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: Little Nell Trent is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: A Dickens heroine hears a bell ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Trent is Little Nell of The Old Curiosity Shop; her first name spoken gives the tolling of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow tolling of a bell, especially at a funeral, is the sound meant.

definitions.meaning: in music the keynote of a scale is called by this name
a reviving drink or medicine that braces you up

explanation.surface: Music has an invigorating effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The keynote of a key in music and a refreshing pick-me-up share the one word.

clue.text: I sit up to speak on the blower in a fury

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the two words are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone sits up to make an angry telephone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I SIT into TISI. One of the Furies of Greek myth is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: She is one of the three Erinyes, the avenging Furies of Greek myth.

clue.text: Cats if fed like this cause alienation

indicators.note: like this tells us to rearrange the preceding words into the form wanted

explanation.surface: Feeding cats this way would make them estranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like this' signals that CATS IF FED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone, making them discontented and unfriendly, is to cause alienation.

clue.text: Len met Ron having trouble signing on

indicators.note: having trouble suggests the three names are in disorder and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Two men have difficulty when they meet to register.
explanation.definitionFit: Registering as a member or student is signing on.

clue.text: What's metal with three feet and two arms? A weighty matter

definitions.text: What's metal with three feet and two arms? A weighty matter

parts.note: steel is a metal alloy of iron
a yard is a length of three feet

explanation.surface: A riddle about a metal object with three feet and two arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'feet' are a measure of length, not legs; the 'two arms' are the unequal arms of a balance, and the 'weighty matter' is weighing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a weighing balance with a beam of two unequal arms and a sliding weight.

clue.text: A bottle needed when Mum comes up with draw, only one

indicators.note: comes up in a down clue means the word for mother is read upwards

parts.note: Ma is mother
to pull is to draw
A is one, a single thing

explanation.surface: A bottle is needed when Mother comes up with a draw ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-handled flask used by the Romans, or a church vessel for holy oil, is a kind of bottle.

annotationWithheld.why: The matchless one with a copper-top (7) (feed's '8' is a misread of 'a'): 'The matchless one' is ORINDA, Katherine Philips's sobriquet 'the Matchless Orinda', with D (copper) on top; no clue word defines DORINDA except 'one', which is also part of the sobriquet

parts.note: looks like a killer who is blameless, but means the king who ordered the Massacre of the Innocents in the Gospel of Matthew

explanation.surface: A killer who is not guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent' seems to describe the murderer; it is his victims, the infants of Bethlehem.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Judea ordered the killing of Bethlehem's infant boys, the Holy Innocents.

clue.text: For music on the Italian level ?

definitions.meaning: a direction in a score meaning play softly
Italian for a floor or storey

explanation.surface: An instrument for music on a particular floor of an Italian house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For music' tempts the instrument; it is the score marking for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian gives music its marking for softly, and the same Italian word names a storey of a building.

clue.text: The curtain is up in the old borough

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the act of the play is in progress
a former municipal borough of west London

explanation.surface: Theatre curtain rises in a historic town.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton was a Middlesex municipal borough until it became part of the London Borough of Ealing in 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: When the curtain rises the act is on, and the same letters name a former borough of west London.

parts.note: reads as curves of a capricious person, but means the paths traced by things in flight, like a thrown ball

explanation.surface: A curvy, flirtatious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectile's flight path traces this kind of curve, the shape of a conic section.

parts.note: reads as ugly sights, but means sore swellings on the eyelid

explanation.surface: Ugly things spoiling the view.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyesore is usually an ugly building; here it is a literal sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed swellings at the edge of an eyelid are literally sores of the eye.

clue.text: Gush like a grateful departing patient

definitions.meaning: a cured patient goes out of hospital in good health

explanation.surface: A thankful patient pours out praise on leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowing forth like a spring is gushing, and a cured patient is leaving in good health.

definitions.meaning: a convent, a place of religious seclusion for women
Hamlet tells Ophelia 'Get thee to' this place

explanation.surface: Hamlet advises a retreat from the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is a house of religious seclusion, and Hamlet urges Ophelia to go to one.

indicators.note: in tells us the bird is found inside the letters of the place name

explanation.surface: A bird spotted in a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a bird, so a flier.

parts.note: Malachi is the last of the Old Testament prophets

indicators.note: set back means the letters of set are read in reverse order

explanation.surface: A prophet is delayed by stones being thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back by' reads like being delayed, but 'back' turns the letters of 'set' round and 'by' just joins them to the prophet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Green copper carbonate minerals polished as ornamental stones.
